chapter: Philadelphia, New York and Sam Wooding in Europe
title: Back to New York on the day of the stock market crash
summary: He paid his own way home straight to New York, the last night with Wooding at the Lido in Paris being the night of the crash.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. Now when you left, you left the band in Paris, did you leave and just go straight back to New York or did you --
Yes, straight back to New York.
You didn't play in Paris?
No.
Or join anyone else?
No I just went straight to New York.
Uh-huh. And did you have to pay your own way back?
Yes.
And that was in 1929?
That was the day of the Stock Market
Crash. That was when -- that was -- our last night with Sam at this Lido Club, in Paris, I think it was the Lido, that was the night of the Stock Market Crash.
Oh, really? And so it was still 1929 when you got back?
Uh-huh.
It wasn't in the early '30's --
I guess so, yes.
That was the day of the Stock Market Crash. I'll never forget it.
How did that affect everybody?
Well, it was a shock to everybody. But things continued for awhile, I imagine, over there and then like here, they started to falling like dying out.
That obviously did not discourage you from coming back to the States?

No, I really didn't know what that meant at the time. Stock Market Crash didn't mean a thing to me, I didn't know what it meant. I was worried about -- I wanted to get back and get back in the swing and see what the guys were playing over here.
So you -- you really came back at the worst time, but you --
I came back at the worst time.
